newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NSA DILUTED EARNINGS UP ON HALF-YEAR.
newsitem.headline: NSA DILUTED EARNINGS UP ON HALF-YEAR.

text.p: NSA Investments Ltd on Sunday announced diluted earnings per share up 24 percent from 29 cents to 36 cents for the six months ending December 31, 1996.
"Our deal flow is positive and we will continue to look at large and attractive propositions," company chairman Arnie Witkin said in a statement.
"All of our existing investments are involved in acquisitive growth strategies and new investments are being explored."
He said NSA's strategy was to acquire significant minority interests in high growth listed and unlisted businesses to which it could add strategic value.

The company raised 281 million rand by way of a rights issue in November 1996. Since then it has invested 295 million rand in listed investments, the market value of which had increased by 62 percent to 477 million rand at March 14 this year.
NSA also invested 57 million rand in unlisted investments.
Witkin said diluted net asset value per share had increased by 15 percent from July 1, 1996 to March 14, 1997, and added:
"Nearly all of the unlisted investments are undergoing step changes and a review of the values will be undertaken at the company's financial year-end, June 30, 1997."
Earlier this year, NSA announced the unbundling of its holdings in Education Investment Corp Ltd (Educor) and Housewares Group Ltd , which the company said would yield 169 million rand.

NSA said although all of the rights issue money had been invested, the company expected to receive between 80 and 90 million rand on the exercise of its share options and a 250 million rand finance facility which has been established, making over 300 million rand available for further investment.
